Maya: Heads-up: prepping playback for a customer custody audit next week. Need to confirm evidence ingest format for BYOK HSM handoffs. What's the minimum signed artifacts we should accept? cc: @Jamal @Zoe
Jamal: Do we mean the HSM import envelope + attestation signature? Or also operator logs?
Zoe: We need both: import envelope (DER) w/ attestation chain; operator action log (signed) + timeline. Legal wants immutable auditability.
Maya: Legal asked for tamper-proof chain for 12 months, plus proof-of-possession at import. Also need KMS integration mapping (CMK -> customer-id).
Jamal: For ingest, suggest accept: 1) HSM Import Envelope (.der) 2) attestation.json (signed by vendor) 3) operator_manifest.log (signed) 4) CMK mapping file signed by customer. We hash everything and store SHA256 in AuditDB.
Jamal: Example hash command:
```
shasum -a 256 import-envelope.der | awk '{print $1}'
```
Zoe: Question: who can upload? RBAC change needed so 'custody-ingest' role can write to audit bucket. Currently only 'ops' can. We should create short-lifetime presigned upload; record uploader identity.
Maya: Agree. Proposed RBAC: - system:custody-ingest (can PutObject to s3://custody-evidence) - system:custody-reader (view only). Add policy to deny deletion except by retention-service. Also record KMS-encrypted envelope.
Jamal: Vulnerability note: If attestation signature uses SHA1 we must reject. Enforce signature alg >= SHA256. Add validation step in ingest lambda.
Zoe: Incident flow: if mismatch between imported hash and stored audit hash, auto-open incident in #incidents and quarantine key. Steps: notify customer, freeze CMK, start onboarding rollback.
Maya: I'll write a short spec. Anyone want to review before EOD? cc @sec-bot will run quick schema tests. :eyes:
sec-bot: automated: schema-check passed for example payloads (3/3) :white_check_mark:
Maya: Thanks all. I'll post PR with RBAC policy and sample payloads. :thumbsup:
